# Skills and docs for the agent supervisor (KAN-91, KAN-92)

## What to build

Teach the bundled skills about graph-manager's new run tools and run events, and document the feature. The code is already in the codebase from earlier tasks: graph-manager's MCP tools `list_runs`, `get_run_log`, `get_node_output`, `get_artifacts`, `list_graphs`, `open_run`, `open_graph`, `propose_graph`, `refresh_ui`, `cancel_run`, `resume_run` (files in `apps/graph-manager/src/server/tools/`), the run event watcher in `apps/graph-manager/src/server/supervisor.ts` that types `[graph-manager] …` lines into the agent terminal that started a run, run origins in `apps/graph-manager/src/server/run-origins.ts`, and the per-workspace **Supervisor** setting (`report` default / `act`) in the workspace settings drawer with `GET/PUT /api/workspaces/:id/supervisor`. This task changes only Markdown: two skills (and their copies under `.claude/skills/`), the graph-manager README, and a new wiki page. Read `docs/prd/agent-supervisor.md` first: it is the source for every name and message.

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `docs/prd/agent-supervisor.md` (whole file) — the spec: tool table, event lines, decisions, non-goals.
- `packages/graph-execution/skills/run-graph/SKILL.md` (lines 30–75) — section "5. Launch" mentions `open_start_run`; section "6. Report and stop" is where watching a run is described.
- `packages/graph-execution/skills/to-tasks/SKILL.md` (around line 214) — the "In graph-manager" bullet that calls `open_start_run`.
- `.claude/skills/run-graph/SKILL.md`, `.claude/skills/to-tasks/SKILL.md` — byte-identical copies of the two files above, used when developing this repo. Keep them identical after your edit (copy the files over). Do not touch `.claude/skills/run-graph/SKILL 2.md`.
- `apps/graph-manager/README.md` lines 208–226 ("### Agents and tools", the `The tools:` list with `open_start_run`) and lines 268–293 ("### Adding a tool").
- `docs/wiki/features/agent-tools.md` — the format to copy for the new wiki page (Summary, Decisions table, Known follow-ups, Code references, Related).
- `docs/wiki/index.md` — the feature list; append a link.
- The new tool files in `apps/graph-manager/src/server/tools/` and `apps/graph-manager/src/server/supervisor.ts` — read each tool's `description` and input schema and the exact event line texts so the docs match the code (the code wins over the spec where they differ).

## Patterns to follow

Skill bullets are full sentences, conditional on the tool being available, like the existing one:

```
**In graph-manager, hand the run to the user.** When the user asks to start a run in a graph-manager terminal and the tool `open_start_run` from the `graph-manager` MCP server is in your tools, call it instead of running the CLI: ...
```

Wiki decision tables use columns `Decision | Why | Ticket` with ticket `KAN-91` or `KAN-92`.

## Step-by-step tasks

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/skills/run-graph/SKILL.md`

- **IMPLEMENT**: add a paragraph (in section 5 after the `open_start_run` paragraph, or a new short section before "6. Report and stop") titled **In graph-manager, the run reports back.** Content: when the agent started or resumed a run from a graph-manager terminal, graph-manager types one-line messages starting with `[graph-manager]` into its terminal when the run starts, enters review, succeeds, fails, is resumed or is cancelled. Follow the instruction in a failure line: `Supervisor: report` means tell the user what failed and why and do not change code or rerun; `Supervisor: act` means find the cause with `get_run_log` and `get_node_output`, fix it, commit (agents only see committed code), and call `resume_run` with that run id. Use `list_runs`, `get_run_log`, `get_node_output`, `get_artifacts`, `cancel_run`, `resume_run` and `open_run` when they are in your tools instead of reading `.graph-execution/` files or polling `state.json` in a sleep loop. After a run succeeds, call `open_run` so the user sees it.
- **GOTCHA**: keep the outside-graph-manager instructions unchanged.

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/skills/to-tasks/SKILL.md`

- **IMPLEMENT**: in the "In graph-manager" bullet: when `propose_graph` is in your tools, call it (same arguments as `open_start_run`: `tasksDir`, `spec`) instead of `open_start_run`; it shows the graph to the user, who approves (the Start run form opens) or rejects (you get `[graph-manager] The user rejected the graph <tasksDir>.` in the terminal; ask the user what to change). Otherwise use `open_start_run` as today.

### COPY to `.claude/skills/`

- **IMPLEMENT**: `cp packages/graph-execution/skills/run-graph/SKILL.md .claude/skills/run-graph/SKILL.md` and the same for `to-tasks`.
- **VALIDATE**: `diff packages/graph-execution/skills/run-graph/SKILL.md .claude/skills/run-graph/SKILL.md && diff packages/graph-execution/skills/to-tasks/SKILL.md .claude/skills/to-tasks/SKILL.md`

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/README.md`

- **IMPLEMENT**: under "The tools:" add one bullet per new tool with its input and what it does (copy the style of the `open_start_run` bullet). Add a subsection `#### Run events and the Supervisor setting` explaining: which terminal gets events (the agent terminal that started or resumed the run; dropped when it was closed, isn't an agent terminal, or the agent has quit to the shell), the six event lines verbatim from `supervisor.ts`, typing only after 3 s of quiet, and the Supervisor setting (workspace settings drawer: "Report to me" / "Fix and rerun"; `GET/PUT /api/workspaces/:id/supervisor`; no cap on reruns). Note that runs started from the UI without an agent request have no origin and send no events.

### CREATE `docs/wiki/features/agent-supervisor.md`

- **IMPLEMENT**: title `# Agent supervisor: run tools and run events for terminal agents (KAN-91, KAN-92)`. Summary (spec: `docs/prd/agent-supervisor.md`; tasks: `.agents/tasks/agent-supervisor/`). Decisions table `Decision | Why | Ticket` from the spec's Decisions (PTY typing; origin terminal only; drop rules; in-memory origins; shim picks the run id; 2 s polling of origin runs; run-level events; Supervisor setting default report; mode text in the failure line; UI tools on the agent-request queue; open_graph/propose_graph; cancel via /abort; resume without answers; own-workspace scope). Known follow-ups: machine-wide status (opt-in), origins and queued events lost on restart, `--resume` without `--run` in a terminal gets no origin, suites not supervised, no Windows MCP shim, dictated answers on resume. Code references: every new file. Related: link `agent-tools.md`, `graph-manager.md`, `../index.md`.

### UPDATE `docs/wiki/index.md`

- **IMPLEMENT**: append `- [Agent supervisor: run tools and run events for terminal agents (KAN-91, KAN-92)](features/agent-supervisor.md)` at the end of the Features list.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `run-graph` SKILL.md mentions `[graph-manager]`, `Supervisor: act`, `resume_run`, `get_run_log`, `get_node_output`, `open_run`.
- [ ] `to-tasks` SKILL.md mentions `propose_graph` and falls back to `open_start_run`.
- [ ] `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` are identical to `packages/graph-execution/skills/*/SKILL.md` for run-graph and to-tasks.
- [ ] README lists all 12 tools and documents the Supervisor setting; event lines match `supervisor.ts` exactly.
- [ ] Wiki page exists and is linked from `docs/wiki/index.md`.
- [ ] `npm test -w graph-execution -- skills` and `npm test -w graph-manager -- skills` still pass (skills are installed from these files).

## Validation commands

```bash
npm run typecheck && npm run lint
npm test -w graph-execution -- skills
npm test -w graph-manager -- skills
diff packages/graph-execution/skills/run-graph/SKILL.md .claude/skills/run-graph/SKILL.md
diff packages/graph-execution/skills/to-tasks/SKILL.md .claude/skills/to-tasks/SKILL.md
```
